comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 OER Appendix3 p31 and the official year pages agree on one 180-EC framework: 60EC compulsory first year; 48EC compulsory second year plus12EC from four listed restricted options; and18EC compulsory advanced study,30EC genuine free choice in third-year semester1 and a12EC thesis. Retain the first two restricted options in the published list, Security in the Netherlands and Challenges in Policy Advising, selected neutrally before UCR matching and subject to capacity. No named route is required. Appendix4 pp32–33 explicitly accepts current replacements for the older methods prerequisites: thesis entry is90EC including Academic Skills, Public Administration Research Methodology and Applied Quantitative Methods. This sequence satisfies the conditions. European Governance excludes MAN-BCU348A, which is not selected. Free-space choices require approval/non-overlap; internships can be6,12or18EC and require90EC including the full first year. Mandatory academic Dutch language testing carries no additional credits. BSA normally42of60EC; attendance, interim work and proposal conditions apply as recorded in component notes. Appendix4 repeats BPRA201 next to quantitative methods, but Appendix3 and the current year-page course link unambiguously identify the separate quantitative unit as BPRA200; no unit or credit is duplicated. This is the current published framework; future offerings may change. Fresh1November2026 confirms all25positions180EC/current44-pageOERAppendix3/4 andcurrentyearpages. Current explicitthesisreplacementconditions accepted, unlike unresolvedconditions in othercases; no inheritedcasefailure applied. Current BPRA200 identityconfirmedseparatelyfromduplicatedAppendix4BPRA201label. Fresh41interestreview confirms directpoverty/welfare concern can be owned by closestpubliceconomics/inequality/policycore; housing-specificdirection separately challenged, not rejected for oldmissingofferings. Current PublicPolicyAnalysis now has2028h1/2029h1offering and is included in allthreecurricula. No oldavailability judgment retained. Allactualcourses/readerfields reassessed; newleadershipunderpressurecontent supported, obsolete diversity-managementtitle notused.

core: Public policy, government institutions and the governance of societal problems
Public organisations, citizens, law, politics, economics and public values
Policy formation, implementation, evaluation and evidence-based problem solving
Quantitative, qualitative and independent research into policy and governance
Policy advice, communication and democratic engagement
adjacent: Public organisations, leadership and digital governance
questions: Why do some policies work while others fail, and how can public problems be addressed?
How can governments respond to climate change and sustainability transitions?
How can public organisations be governed, led and adapted in a digital age?

trace: AI, organisations and governance: national AI readiness, workforce, industrial policy and regulation alongside business/economic cases. Material digital-governance methods, without claiming a complete e-government or public-service design syllabus.
introduces economic reasoning about markets, institutions and government choices
examines macroeconomic conditions and policy in an international setting
analyses incentives and behavioural mechanisms shaping individual and policy outcomes

Direct public-policy economics: market failure, public goods, externalities, collective choice, public spending/taxation, welfare, social insurance and redistribution, with research proposal/paper. Substantively supports poverty/public-policy interest, not a dedicated housing-market course.
provides econometric methods for evaluating relationships and policy-relevant evidence
provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis
develops ethical leadership communication and persuasive practice

Organisational leadership under conflict and exclusion: emotion regulation, identity/belonging and psychological safety, inclusive leadership and an actual supervised survey with original data and statistical analysis. This is not a generic diversity-management curriculum or dedicated public-sector management course.

Actual organisational behaviour, groups, motivation, structure/culture/change, research design and PRISMA-guided evidence synthesis. These are relevant to public organisations but do not establish all public-sector management/accountability rules.

Negotiation through interest-based bargaining, power/emotion/trust/culture and repeated simulations, ending with a Delta Climate Center negotiation scenario. Provides specific stakeholder methods, not a full policy-process theory.
Complementary empirical tools: cleaning, manipulating and visualising tabular, spatial and text data, with a research project across disciplines. Public-policy datasets are not guaranteed.
directly studies institutions, participation and policy for sustainability transitions
Complementary environmental framework: planetary boundaries identify the environmental limits within which policy and governance choices are made; this is not public administration training.

Direct thematic grounding for climate policy: scientific drivers, environmental and societal impacts, adaptation, mitigation, interest-group misinformation, climate governance and justice are studied together.
Complementary assessment method: life-cycle impacts of products, processes and services and circular-economy planning inform environmental policy trade-offs. This is not a policy-process course.
examines how law structures social relations, institutions and justice
compares constitutional institutions, public authority and democratic arrangements
examines EU institutions, legal authority and multilevel governance

Moral reasoning through historical/contemporary ethical theories, interpretation and practical ethical argument. Supports public-value judgments without claiming a dedicated administrative-ethics syllabus or specific climate-policy content.
provides comparative analysis of political institutions, regimes and government

EU institutions, representation, agenda setting, legislation and implementation, with real EuropeanParliament amendment coding/research. Direct multilevel-governance inquiry; not complete Dutch domestic administration.

Complementary conflict-governance analysis: regional, national and international cases examine structural inequality, ideology, colonial grievances, institutions and civil-society peacebuilding. No Dutch public-safety organisation syllabus is claimed.
introduces social institutions, inequality and the analysis of societal problems
develops qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity

Complementary social theory: modernity, imperialism, colonial responses and debates in sociology contextualise public institutions and inequality. This is not a dedicated citizen–government relations course.
examines collective action, environmental justice and political mobilisation

Direct public-sphere and civil-society analysis: Gramsci, Habermas, Fraser, solidarity, civil repair and decolonial critiques frame an empirical NGO or civil-society organisation study. Government agencies are not guaranteed project subjects.

Complementary behavioural foundations: scientific social psychology examines how the presence of others shapes thought, feelings and behaviour; application to citizen behaviour is supplied by the programme.

Complementary academic and professional communication: rhetorical analysis, argument, writing and oral presentation support public and organisational communication; no dedicated policy-advice project is guaranteed.
examines how climate problems are framed and communicated to publics

Direct public-communication method: framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and persuasion ethics are applied in a local-institution communication project. This supports the communication dimension of advice, not the whole policy-advising process.

Direct public-law context: sources and institutions of public international law, state authority, treaties, compliance, refugee and environmental law support analysis of public organisations beyond the national state. This does not reproduce comparative public-administration practice.

Direct public-policy inquiry through policy-making phases and alternative conceptualisations across national and international arenas, examined through a sugar case with policy memos. Description supports these capacities; no comprehensive Dutch policy implementation, evaluation or housing-specific syllabus is inferred.

selection.assessment: Three substantive programmes address public policy/institutions, climate governance and public organisations/digital change with actual policy analysis now included. The closest core substantively addresses poverty through public economics/welfare/redistribution and sociological inequality; it owns1719 rather than pretending a separate welfare option. Housing1718 remains a genuine candidate question: current PublicPolicyAnalysis is considered fully and is feasible, but its sugar/globalpolicy case does not establish sustained housing-policy/market/development content. PublicEconomics,propertylaw andSpatialPlanning give general publicgoods/property/geospatial tools, not a strong separate housing programme; this is a content judgment, not an old-offering exclusion or a degree-title test. Climate has distinct governance/justice/communication and science-grounded policy tradeoffs; organisations has specific leadership-underpressure/survey, rhetoric/communication, publicinternational law andAIregulatory inquiry while retaining publiceconomics/policy. All three pass materialtargetsubstance, coherence, academic progression and distinctness gates. Current pairwise differences: [{'pair': [1, 2], 'differentCoursesEach': 7, 'differentEC': 52.5}, {'pair': [1, 3], 'differentCoursesEach': 5, 'differentEC': 37.5}, {'pair': [2, 3], 'differentCoursesEach': 7, 'differentEC': 52.5}]. Maximum reached only after these tests.

notes.text: These UCR routes offer substantial political, legal, economic, social and organisational analysis with empirical methods. Radboud provides a dedicated public-administration sequence in policy formation and implementation, Dutch administration, public-sector practice, digital government and a separate 12-EC thesis. UCR does not reproduce every specialist unit; optional independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-taught Public Administration degree studies how policy, government and public organisations shape societal problems, and how their effects can be understood and improved. It combines political, legal, economic and social perspectives with empirical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR routes combine public-policy analysis and empirical methods with institutions, climate governance, or public organisations and leadership. Radboud adds a dedicated Dutch public-administration sequence, specialist policy implementation and a separate bachelor thesis. The UCR routes develop related academic capacities and do not confer the same disciplinary qualification.
